name: Ugali
description: A stiff dough of maize flour (sometimes cassava, sorghum or millet) cooked in boiling water until firm. It is Kenya's everyday starch, served with greens, stews, fish or grilled meat. Kenya's version of the maize staple called pap in South Africa.
how_to_eat: Pinch off a piece with your fingers, press a dent in it with your thumb and use it to scoop up the stew or greens.
how_to_order: Served at roadhouses and budget eateries everywhere, usually as the starch alongside a stew or meat.

name: Sukuma wiki
description: Collard greens (sukuma) sautéed in oil with onions and seasoning; the name means "push the week" because the greens are cheap and available all year. It is the standard side to ugali; some cooks add meat or fish.
how_to_eat: Eat as a side with ugali.
how_to_order: Ask whether it is cooked with meat or meat stock if you are vegetarian; Lonely Planet notes many vegetable dishes are.

name: Nyama choma
description: Grilled meat, usually goat, sometimes beef, cooked over wood or charcoal; the name means "grilled meat" in Swahili. Often called an unofficial national dish, it is eaten at roadside joints and gatherings with ugali and kachumbari.
how_to_eat: Eat with your hands, alongside ugali and kachumbari.
how_to_order: Ordered by weight at grill joints and cafés; Lonely Planet suggests a half-kilo portion.

name: Kachumbari
description: An uncooked relish of chopped tomatoes, onions and chilli, with lemon juice or vinegar and salt. The name comes from the Indian word cachumber; in Kenya it is served with nyama choma, pilau and mukimo.
how_to_eat: Eat as a fresh side with grilled meat, pilau or ugali.
how_to_order: Comes as a side with nyama choma and rice dishes.

name: Kenyan chapati
description: The East African chapati is a layered wheat flatbread fried in oil, butter or lard, closer to a thin paratha than the Indian chapati; it came with Indian railway workers. Unlike the Indian chapati puffed over a flame, it is fried and layered.
how_to_eat: Tear pieces to scoop up stews, beans or greens, or eat with tea.
how_to_order: Sold at street stalls and canteens; ask if it is cooked with oil if you avoid lard or butter.

name: Mandazi
description: A lightly sweet fried bread, often triangular, that is a principal dish of Swahili coastal cooking and now a standard breakfast across Kenya. It is made from wheat dough with yeast or baking powder; many Kenyan recipes add milk, butter and egg.
how_to_eat: Eat fresh in the morning with a cup of chai.
how_to_order: Sold at kiosks and cafés from early morning.

name: Kenyan chai
description: Sweet, milky black tea, often boiled together with milk and sugar, sometimes with ginger or masala spices. Many Kenyans start the day with it, usually with a mandazi; Kalenjin tea is often around 40% milk.
how_to_eat: Drink hot with mandazi or chapati.
how_to_order: Ask for chai at any café or kiosk; black tea without milk is called chai ya rangi.

name: Smocha
description: A street wrap of a smokie (sausage) rolled in a chapati with kachumbari and a sauce of your choice; also called chapo smokie. It is sold from roadside stalls in Kenya's cities.
how_to_order: Ask a roadside smokie vendor for a smocha. Price was KES 60-70 in 2023 (Citizen Digital).

name: Mayai pasua
description: A boiled egg split and served with a salad of tomatoes, onions and pepper, sold by street vendors in Nairobi's CBD along with smokies. It is a quick snack between meals.
how_to_order: Buy from smokie and egg carts in Nairobi CBD.

name: Dawa
description: A Kenyan cocktail of vodka, lime and honey; dawa means "medicine" in Swahili. Lonely Planet lists it among Kenya's local cocktail creations.
how_to_order: Order at bars; contains alcohol.

name: Kenyan pilau
description: Rice cooked with spices such as cloves, cardamom, cinnamon and black pepper, usually with meat, potatoes and onions. A cornerstone of Swahili coastal cooking that is now found across Kenya, it is often kept for special occasions and served with kachumbari. This is the Kenyan version of pilaf.
how_to_eat: Eat with kachumbari.
how_to_order: Sold at Swahili eateries and street lunch stalls on the coast.

name: Swahili biryani
description: A coastal rice dish where the spiced meat or chicken sauce and the rice are cooked separately, unlike pilau, often with potatoes. Chicken biryani (biryani kuku) with tamarind (ukwaju) juice and kachumbari is the best-selling coastal street lunch. The dish came to the coast from South Asia through trade.
how_to_order: Ask for biryani kuku (chicken biryani) at Swahili lunch spots and street stalls.

name: Viazi karai
description: Boiled, peeled potatoes dipped in a gram (chickpea) flour batter, sometimes mixed with wheat flour, and deep-fried in a karai, a basin-like pan. It is a Mombasa afternoon snack, served with tamarind sauce, chilli or coconut chutney.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with tamarind sauce or coconut chutney.
how_to_order: Buy from Swahili women vendors in the alleys of Mombasa's Old Town, usually in the late afternoon.

name: Mahamri
description: A coastal fried bread made from wheat dough with yeast, sugar, cardamom and coconut milk. It is a Swahili breakfast staple, usually eaten with mbaazi; most people buy it from street vendors rather than make it at home.
how_to_eat: Eat with mbaazi wa nazi and spiced tea for breakfast.
how_to_order: Buy fresh from breakfast vendors early; they often sell out by mid-morning.

name: Mbaazi wa nazi
description: Pigeon peas cooked in coconut milk. Paired with mahamri, it is the classic Swahili breakfast along the Kenyan coast.
how_to_eat: Dip mahamri into the peas.
how_to_order: Sold by breakfast vendors on the coast.

name: Mishkaki
description: Cubes of marinated beef or chicken skewered and grilled over charcoal, sold by the stick, with tamarind sauce and salad. It is mostly an evening street food in Mombasa.
how_to_order: Buy by the stick from evening grills; some vendors add chips, naan or chapati.

name: Kuku paka
description: Chicken that is char-grilled and then cooked in a coconut milk curry sauce; also called kuku na nazi. It has African, Indian and Arab influences and is popular on the coast; fish or shrimp versions exist.
how_to_eat: Eat over rice such as wali wa nazi (coconut rice) or with chapati and sukuma wiki.

name: Samaki wa kupaka
description: Whole fish, such as red snapper or kingfish, coated in a sauce of coconut milk, tamarind, pepper and turmeric. On Lamu it is made for special occasions such as weddings and is especially popular during Ramadan.
how_to_eat: Serve with rice or bread; during Ramadan it is eaten with a millet or wheat porridge.

name: Kahawa chungu
description: Strong Swahili black coffee, similar to Arabic coffee but with a strong clove and black pepper aroma; chungu means bitter. It is a coastal drink, often taken with sweet snacks.
how_to_eat: Drink with a sweet snack such as mitai.

name: Madafu
description: Young green coconuts opened for their water; after drinking, the soft white flesh is eaten. It is the standard coastal refreshment, sold at places like Mama Ngina Drive in Mombasa.
how_to_eat: Drink the water, then scoop out the flesh.

name: Swahili halwa
description: A jelly-like sweet made from starch, sugar, cardamom and ghee, garnished with cashew nuts or almonds. It is sold by sweet vendors in Mombasa and Lamu.

name: Mabuyu
description: Baobab seeds cooked in sugar syrup and coloured, usually red but also green, yellow or purple. It is a coastal snack sold around Mackinnon Market in Mombasa.

name: Githeri
description: Maize kernels and beans boiled together in a pot (sufuria), sometimes stewed with onions, tomatoes, potatoes or meat. It is a staple of the Kikuyu, Meru, Embu and Kamba and has been the standard Kenyan school meal since the 1920s.
how_to_order: Ask whether it is cooked with meat if you are vegetarian.

name: Mukimo
description: Potatoes mashed with green vegetables such as pumpkin leaves or peas, sometimes with maize and beans; also called irio. It comes from communities around Mount Kenya and is served with stew or nyama choma.
how_to_eat: Eat as a side with beef stew or nyama choma.

name: Uji
description: A thin porridge of millet, maize or sorghum flour, served warm, often with milk and sugar. The Kikuyu make a fermented version called ũcũrũ.
how_to_eat: Drink warm from a cup at breakfast.
how_to_order: Ask whether it is made with milk if you avoid dairy.

name: Mutura
description: A blood sausage of intestine casing stuffed with chopped beef or goat meat, tripe and cooked blood, seasoned with onion, salt, pepper and chilli, then grilled. It is a Kikuyu dish now sold by street vendors, especially in Nairobi; some versions leave out the blood.
how_to_order: Buy from roadside street vendors.

name: Ugali with fried tilapia
description: Whole tilapia from Lake Victoria, fried, stewed in tomato, onion and garlic or grilled over charcoal, served with ugali and greens. Fish with ugali is the everyday meal of the Luo around Kisumu.
how_to_eat: Pull the fish apart with your fingers and scoop it up with ugali.
how_to_order: Order at the fish stalls on Dunga Beach outside Kisumu.

name: Omena
description: Small silver cyprinid fish from Lake Victoria, sun-dried and cooked with tomatoes and onions, sometimes with peanut sauce. It is a Luo staple usually eaten with ugali.
how_to_eat: Eat with ugali and greens.

name: Aliya
description: Strips of sun-dried beef, later stewed with tomato and onion or fried until crisp. It is a traditional Luo dish.
how_to_eat: Eat with ugali or chapati.

name: Ingokho
description: Chicken prepared by the Luhya and eaten with ugali, a favourite meal in Western Kenya. It is served to distinguished guests, and a cockerel is slaughtered and cooked at dowry ceremonies.
how_to_eat: Eat with ugali.

name: Mrenda
description: Jute leaves cooked as a green vegetable, also called murere, eaten by the Luhya. It is served with ugali.
how_to_eat: Scoop up with ugali.

name: Osuga
description: A slightly bitter leafy green, the best-loved of the traditional Luo vegetables. It is eaten with ugali, often alongside fish.
how_to_eat: Eat as a side with ugali and fish.

name: Matoke
description: Green cooking bananas (East African Highland bananas), stewed with onions, tomatoes and spices, often with beef. Cooking bananas are a staple around the Lake Victoria area of Kenya.
how_to_eat: Eat with chapati.
how_to_order: Ask if it is cooked with beef if you are vegetarian.

name: Mursik
description: Cow's or goat's milk fermented for several days in a gourd (sotet) lined with charcoal from specific trees, which flavours it. It is the traditional drink of the Kalenjin, served at dowry ceremonies and to returning athletes; in the past blood was sometimes added, which is now rare.
how_to_eat: Drink at room temperature or chilled, alone or with ugali.

name: Psong'iot
description: Kalenjin ugali made from millet and sorghum flour instead of maize; maize ugali is called kimnyet. It is served with greens and milk.
how_to_eat: Eat with socheek or other vegetables.

name: Socheek
description: A Kalenjin vegetable relish of greens cooked with milk and cream. It is a typical side for ugali.
how_to_eat: Eat with ugali.

name: Mcheleng
description: Rice cooked with milk into a creamy dish, made by the Kalenjin as a treat for children and eaten by the whole family.

name: Moriot
description: The crust left in the pot after cooking ugali, eaten as a snack by the Kalenjin.
